record.paper_title: A General Framework for Coloring Problems: Old Results, New Results, and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Planar backbone coloring with spanning-tree backbones
record.original_question: For every planar graph G and every spanning tree T of G used as a backbone, is the backbone coloring number at most 6? Equivalently, can the known universal upper bound bbc(G,T) <= 7, obtained from the 4-Color Theorem and the general spanning-tree bound, always be improved by one?

evidence.quote: bbc(G,T) <= 7 holds for any planar graph G with spanning tree T.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V, E) be a finite simple graph and let H be a spanning subgraph of G (the "backbone"). A backbone coloring of (G, H) is a proper vertex coloring c : V → {1, 2, 3, ...} such that |c(u) − c(v)| ≥ 2 for every edge uv of H (while |c(u) − c(v)| ≥ 1 is required for every edge uv of G). The backbone chromatic number bbc(G, H) is the smallest integer k such that there exists a backbone coloring of (G, H) using colors from {1, 2, ..., k}.

Prove or disprove: for every planar graph G and every spanning tree T of G,
    bbc(G, T) ≤ 6.

(Equivalently, can the universal upper bound bbc(G, T) ≤ 7 — which follows from the Four Color Theorem combined with the general spanning-tree bound bbc(G, T) ≤ 2χ(G) − 1 — always be improved by one when G is planar?)
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture, due to Broersma et al. (2007), that bbc(G,T) ≤ 6 for every planar graph G with spanning tree T appears to remain open in general. Partial results are known: it has been proved when T has diameter at most four, and related circular-backbone variants have been studied. There exist planar graphs with a Hamiltonian-path backbone achieving bbc = 6, showing the bound (if true) is tight. No source found claiming a complete resolution.

status_evidence.title: Backbone colouring: Tree backbones with small diameter in planar graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Broersma et al. conjectured that BBC(G,T) ≤ 6 for every planar graph G and every spanning tree T of G. We prove this conjecture when T has diameter at most four.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is stated explicitly and only proved for the special case of trees of diameter ≤ 4.

status_evidence.title: Circular Backbone Colorings: on matching and tree backbones of planar graphs
status_evidence.snippet: It is conjectured that the upper bound can be improved to 7 when H is a tree, and to 6 when H is a matching... partial results are obtained.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work continues to refer to the bound as a conjecture, indicating it is still open.

status_evidence.title: Backbone coloring for graphs with degree 4
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2024) paper on backbone coloring continuing to study the conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Ongoing research treats the planar spanning-tree bound bbc ≤ 6 as an open conjecture.
